items.followUp: State two roles of apoptosis in the body.

rubric.why: Apoptosis removes cells that are damaged or no longer needed.
rubric.description: Identifies the removal of damaged or unneeded cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that apoptosis removes or destroys damaged or unnecessary cells.

rubric.why: Apoptosis helps shape body structures during development and can maintain tissue cell numbers.
rubric.description: Gives a developmental or tissue-maintenance advantage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid advantage, such as shaping body parts by removing cells between developing fingers.

modelAnswer: Apoptosis removes damaged, unwanted or extra cells from the body.
It helps in the normal development and shaping of body parts, for example, by separating developing fingers and toes.

items.followUp: Explain why an enzyme usually acts on only one particular substrate.

rubric.why: Specificity means that an enzyme acts on a particular substrate or a limited type of substrate.
rubric.description: States that an enzyme acts on a specific substrate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the substrate as specific or particular.

rubric.why: The enzyme's active site has a shape that matches its substrate.
rubric.description: Relates specificity to the enzyme's active site or shape.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the substrate fits or matches the active site.

modelAnswer: Specificity of enzymes is the property by which an enzyme acts only on a particular substrate.
This is because the enzyme's active site has a shape complementary to that substrate.

items.followUp: Write the enzyme-action equation and identify the enzyme-substrate complex.

rubric.why: The first stage is the binding of the substrate to the enzyme to form an enzyme-substrate complex.
rubric.description: Shows enzyme and substrate forming the enzyme-substrate complex.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the E + S ⇌ ES part or its correctly labelled equivalent.

rubric.why: The complex forms product, while the enzyme is released unchanged.
rubric.description: Shows the complex forming product and releasing the enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the ES → E + P part or its correctly labelled equivalent.

modelAnswer: Enzyme action can be represented by the equation: E + S ⇌ ES → E + P.
Here, E is enzyme, S is substrate, ES is the enzyme-substrate complex and P is product.

items.followUp: What is ATP made of, and how does it supply energy to a cell?

rubric.why: ATP stands for adenosine triphosphate and is an energy-rich compound in cells.
rubric.description: Defines ATP by its full name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the full form, adenosine triphosphate.

rubric.why: ATP supplies energy for cellular work.
rubric.description: States a use or role of ATP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ATP provides energy for cellular activities or giving a valid example.

modelAnswer: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is an energy-rich compound found in cells and is the cell's energy currency.
It supplies energy for cellular activities such as active transport, muscle contraction and the synthesis of substances.

items.followUp: Name the main photosynthetic pigments and state what pigments do.

rubric.why: Pigments are coloured substances that absorb light.
rubric.description: Defines pigments by their light-absorbing role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pigments are coloured substances that absorb light.

rubric.why: Photosynthetic pigments include chlorophylls and carotenoids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming chlorophyll a and b, or chlorophyll and carotenoids, or other correct photosynthetic pigments.

modelAnswer: Pigments are coloured substances that absorb light.
The main photosynthetic pigments are chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b and carotenoids (carotenes and xanthophylls).

items.followUp: Where does glycolysis occur, and what is its main product?

rubric.why: Glycolysis is the breakdown or splitting of glucose.
rubric.description: States that glycolysis breaks down glucose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying glucose as the molecule broken down.

rubric.why: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and produces pyruvic acid.
rubric.description: Gives the location or main product of glycolysis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that glycolysis produces pyruvic acid or occurs in the cytoplasm.

modelAnswer: Glycolysis is the breakdown of one glucose molecule into two molecules of pyruvic acid.
It takes place in the cytoplasm of the cell.

items.followUp: Why is dietary fibre important, and name two foods that are good sources of it.

rubric.why: Dietary fibre, or roughage, is the indigestible part of plant food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing fibre as indigestible plant material or roughage.

rubric.why: Fruits, vegetables and whole grains are common fibre sources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving two valid sources, such as fruits and vegetables or whole grains.

modelAnswer: Dietary fibre, also called roughage, is the indigestible part of plant foods.
Its sources include fruits, vegetables and whole-grain foods.

items.followUp: Trace the paths of blood through the right and left sides of the heart.

rubric.why: The right side pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the right side sends deoxygenated blood to the lungs.

rubric.why: The left side pumps oxygenated blood to the body; the heart therefore drives pulmonary and systemic circulations.
rubric.description: Describes the systemic pump or identifies the two circulations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the left side sends oxygenated blood to the body, or for naming both circuits.

modelAnswer: The human heart is called a double pump because its two sides pump blood through two separate circuits.
The right side pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs (pulmonary circulation).
The left side pumps oxygenated blood to the rest of the body (systemic circulation).
